sanskrit: atha tāṃ jātasaṃtāpāṃ tena vākyena mohitām saramā hlādayām āsa pṛtivīṃ dyaur ivāmbhasā
english: Then Saramā comforted her who had grown distressed and bewildered by those words, even as the sky refreshes the earth with water.

sanskrit: tatas tasyā hitaṃ sakhyāś cikīrṣantī sakhī vacaḥ uvāca kāle kālajñā smitapūrvābhibhāṣiṇī
english: Then that friend, wishing to do what was beneficial for her companion, and knowing the right moment, spoke words at the proper time, first smiling before she addressed her.

sanskrit: utsaheyam ahaṃ gatvā tvadvākyam asitekṣaṇe nivedya kuśalaṃ rāme praticchannā nivartitum
english: "O dark-eyed one, I am able to go, convey your message to Rāma, learn of his welfare, and return unseen."

sanskrit: na hi me kramamāṇāyā nirālambe vihāyasi samartho gatim anvetuṃ pavano garuḍo 'pi vā
english: "For when I move through the unsupported sky, neither the wind nor even Garuḍa is capable of tracking my course."

sanskrit: evaṃ bruvāṇāṃ tāṃ sītā saramāṃ punar abravīt madhuraṃ ślakṣṇayā vācā pūrvaśokābhipannayā
english: To Saramā speaking thus, Sītā, overcome by former grief, spoke again in sweet and gentle words.

sanskrit: samarthā gaganaṃ gantum api vā tvaṃ rasātalam avagacchāmy akartavyaṃ kartavyaṃ te madantare
english: "I know that you are capable of going to the sky or even to the netherworld; I understand both what should and should not be done on my behalf."

sanskrit: matpriyaṃ yadi kartavyaṃ yadi buddhiḥ sthirā tava jñātum icchāmi taṃ gatvā kiṃ karotīti rāvaṇaḥ
english: "If you wish to do what pleases me, and if your resolve is firm, I desire you to go and find out what Rāvaṇa is doing."

sanskrit: sa hi māyābalaḥ krūro rāvaṇaḥ śatrurāvaṇaḥ māṃ mohayati duṣṭātmā pītamātreva vāruṇī
english: "For that cruel Rāvaṇa, whose power lies in illusion and who causes the enemy to cry out, bewilders me, wicked-souled as he is, just as wine intoxicates one who has drunk it."

sanskrit: tarjāpayati māṃ nityaṃ bhartsāpayati cāsakṛt rākṣasībhiḥ sughorābhir yā māṃ rakṣanti nityaśaḥ
english: "He has me threatened constantly and frightened repeatedly by the most terrible rākṣasī women who guard me at all times."

sanskrit: udvignā śaṅkitā cāsmi na ca svasthaṃ mano mama tad bhayāc cāham udvignā aśokavanikāṃ gatāḥ
english: "I am anxious and fearful, and my mind finds no peace; it is out of that fear and anxiety that I have come to the Aśoka grove."

sanskrit: yadi nāma kathā tasya niścitaṃ vāpi yad bhavet nivedayethāḥ sarvaṃ tat paro me syād anugrahaḥ
english: "If you were to report to me his counsel and whatever his settled resolve might be, that would be the greatest favor you could do for me."

sanskrit: sā tv evaṃ bruvatīṃ sītāṃ saramā valgubhāṣiṇī uvāca vacanaṃ tasyāḥ spṛśantī bāṣpaviklavam
english: Then Saramā of sweet speech, touching Sītā as she spoke thus, trembling with tears, addressed her in these words.

sanskrit: eṣa te yady abhiprāyas tasmād gacchāmi jānaki gṛhya śatror abhiprāyam upāvṛttāṃ ca paśya mām
english: "If this is your wish, then I shall go, O Jānakī; wait and see me return with knowledge of the enemy's intention."

sanskrit: evam uktvā tato gatvā samīpaṃ tasya rakṣasaḥ śuśrāva kathitaṃ tasya rāvaṇasya samantriṇaḥ
english: Having spoken thus, she went to the vicinity of that rākṣasa and heard what Rāvaṇa was saying together with his ministers.

sanskrit: sā śrutvā niścayaṃ tasya niścayajñā durātmanaḥ punar evāgamat kṣipram aśokavanikāṃ tadā
english: She, who was skilled at discerning resolve, having heard the settled intention of that evil-souled one, quickly came back once more to the Aśoka grove.

sanskrit: sā praviṣṭā punas tatra dadarśa janakātmajām pratīkṣamāṇāṃ svām eva bhraṣṭapadmām iva śriyam
english: Entering there again, she saw the daughter of Janaka waiting for her, like Śrī herself bereft of her lotus.

sanskrit: tāṃ tu sītā punaḥ prāptāṃ saramāṃ valgubhāṣiṇīm pariṣvajya ca susnigdhaṃ dadau ca svayam āsanam
english: Sītā, warmly embracing Saramā of sweet speech who had now returned, herself offered her a seat.

sanskrit: ihāsīnā sukhaṃ sarvam ākhyāhi mama tattvataḥ krūrasya niścayaṃ tasya rāvaṇasya durātmanaḥ
english: "Sit here comfortably and tell me everything truly — the settled resolve of that cruel, evil-souled Rāvaṇa."

sanskrit: evam uktā tu saramā sītayā vepamānayā kathitaṃ sarvam ācaṣṭa rāvaṇasya samantriṇaḥ
english: Thus addressed by Sītā who was trembling, Saramā related everything that had been said by Rāvaṇa together with his ministers.

sanskrit: jananyā rākṣasendro vai tvanmokṣārthaṃ bṛhadvacaḥ aviddhena ca vaidehi mantrivṛddhena bodhitaḥ
english: "The lord of rākṣasas was indeed urged at length by his mother and by the senior minister for the purpose of releasing you, O Vaidehī, and advised by that wise elder of the council."

sanskrit: dīyatām abhisatkṛtya manujendrāya maithilī nidarśanaṃ te paryāptaṃ janasthāne yad adbhutam
english: "'Let Maithilī be honourably given back to the lord of men; the marvel that occurred at Janasthāna is proof enough for you —'

sanskrit: laṅghanaṃ ca samudrasya darśanaṃ ca hanūmataḥ vadhaṃ ca rakṣasāṃ yuddhe kaḥ kuryān mānuṣo bhuvi
english: "'— the crossing of the ocean, the appearance of Hanumān, the slaying of the rākṣasas in battle: what mere mortal man on earth could do these things?'

sanskrit: evaṃ sa mantrivṛddhaiś ca mātrā ca bahu bhāṣitaḥ na tvām utsahate moktum artahm arthaparo yathā
english: "Though he was spoken to at length thus by the elder ministers and by his mother, he does not have the will to release you — like a miser who clings to wealth."

sanskrit: notsahaty amṛto moktuṃ yuddhe tvām iti maithili sāmātyasya nṛśaṃsasya niścayo hy eṣa vartate
english: "'He will not release you without being slain in battle' — this, O Maithilī, is the firm resolve of that cruel one together with his ministers."

sanskrit: tad eṣā susthirā buddhir mṛtyulobhād upasthitā bhayān na śaktas tvāṃ moktum anirastas tu saṃyuge rākṣasānāṃ ca sarveṣām ātmanaś ca vadhena hi
english: "This very firm determination has arisen from his greed driven by death; out of fear he is unable to release you unless he is repelled in battle — and that only through the slaying of all the rākṣasas and of himself."

sanskrit: nihatya rāvaṇaṃ saṃkhye sarvathā niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ pratineṣyati rāmas tvām ayodhyām asitekṣaṇe
english: "Having slain Rāvaṇa in battle by all means with his sharp arrows, Rāma will lead you back to Ayodhyā, O dark-eyed one."

sanskrit: etasminn antare śabdo bherīśaṅkhasamākulaḥ śruto vai sarvasainyānāṃ kampayan dharaṇītalam
english: In the meantime, the sound filled with the tumult of kettledrums and conches was heard throughout all the armies, making the earth tremble.

sanskrit: śrutvā tu taṃ vānarasainyaśabdaṃ laṅkāgatā rākṣasarājabhṛtyāḥ naṣṭaujaso dainyaparītaceṣṭāḥ śreyo na paśyanti nṛpasya doṣaiḥ
english: Hearing that sound of the vānara army, the servants of the rākṣasa king stationed in Laṅkā, their energy gone and their movements overcome by despondency, saw no good outcome — owing to the king's faults.

sanskrit: tena śaṅkhavimiśreṇa bherīśabdena rāghavaḥ upayato mahābāhū rāmaḥ parapuraṃjayaḥ
english: To the sound of those kettledrums mingled with conches, Rāghava, the mighty-armed Rāma, conqueror of enemy cities, drew near.

sanskrit: taṃ ninādaṃ niśamyātha rāvaṇo rākṣaseśvaraḥ muhūrtaṃ dhyānam āsthāya sacivān abhyudaikṣata
english: Upon hearing that tumult, Rāvaṇa, lord of the rākṣasas, sat in contemplation for a moment and then looked up at his ministers.

sanskrit: atha tān sacivāṃs tatra sarvān ābhāṣya rāvaṇaḥ sabhāṃ saṃnādayan sarvām ity uvāca mahābalaḥ
english: Then the greatly powerful Rāvaṇa, addressing all those ministers there and making the entire assembly resound, spoke thus.

sanskrit: taraṇaṃ sāgarasyāpi vikramaṃ balasaṃcayam yad uktavanto rāmasya bhavantas tan mayā śrutam bhavataś cāpy ahaṃ vedmi yuddhe satyaparākramān
english: "What you have reported regarding Rāma — the crossing of the ocean, his prowess, and the massing of his forces — I have heard; and I too know you to be those whose valour in battle is true."

sanskrit: tatas tu sumahāprājño mālyavān nāma rākṣasaḥ rāvaṇasya vacaḥ śrutvā mātuḥ paitāmaho 'bravīt
english: Then a rākṣasa of very great wisdom named Mālyavān, the maternal great-grandfather of Rāvaṇa, having heard Rāvaṇa's words, spoke.

sanskrit: vidyāsv abhivinīto yo rājā rājan nayānugaḥ sa śāsti ciram aiśvaryam arīṃś ca kurute vaśe
english: "O king, a king who is well trained in the sciences and follows sound statecraft rules his sovereignty long and brings his enemies under control."

sanskrit: saṃdadhāno hi kālena vigṛhṇaṃś cāribhiḥ saha svapakṣavardhanaṃ kurvan mahad aiśvaryam aśnute
english: "For one who makes peace at the right time, who fights with enemies when necessary, and who strengthens his own side, enjoys great sovereignty."

sanskrit: hīyamānena kartavyo rājñā saṃdhiḥ samena ca na śatrum avamanyeta jyāyān kurvīta vigraham
english: "A king who is weak should make peace, and even one who is equal in strength should do so; one should not despise an enemy, but one who is stronger may resort to open war."

sanskrit: tan mahyaṃ rocate saṃdhiḥ saha rāmeṇa rāvaṇa yadartham abhiyuktāḥ sma sītā tasmai pradīyatām
english: "Therefore, O Rāvaṇa, a treaty with Rāma seems right to me; the Sītā for whose sake we have been assailed should be given back to him."

sanskrit: tasya devarṣayaḥ sarve gandharvāś ca jayaiṣiṇaḥ virodhaṃ mā gamas tena saṃdhis te tena rocatām
english: "All the divine sages and the gandharvas desire his victory; do not come into conflict with him — let a treaty with him be pleasing to you."

sanskrit: asṛjad bhagavān pakṣau dvāv eva hi pitāmahaḥ surāṇām asurāṇāṃ ca dharmādharmau tadāśrayau
english: "For the venerable Pitāmaha created only two sides — that of the suras and that of the asuras — and upon these rested Dharma and Adharma respectively."

sanskrit: dharmo hi śrūyate pakṣaḥ surāṇāṃ ca mahātmanām adharmo rakṣasaṃ pakṣo hy asurāṇāṃ ca rāvaṇa
english: "Dharma is indeed said to be the side of the suras and the great-souled ones; Adharma is the side of the rākṣasas and the asuras, O Rāvaṇa."

sanskrit: dharmo vai grasate 'dharmaṃ tataḥ kṛtam abhūd yugam adharmo grasate dharmaṃ tatas tiṣyaḥ pravartate
english: "When Dharma swallows Adharma, the Kṛta age comes into being; when Adharma swallows Dharma, the Tiṣya (Kali) age commences."

sanskrit: tat tvayā caratā lokān dharmo vinihato mahān adharmaḥ pragṛhītaś ca tenāsmadbalinaḥ pare
english: "By your ranging through the worlds, great Dharma has been destroyed and Adharma has been embraced; on that account the others — our adversaries — have grown stronger than us."

sanskrit: sa pramādād vivṛddhas te 'dharmo 'hir grasate hi naḥ vivardhayati pakṣaṃ ca surāṇāṃ surabhāvanaḥ
english: "That Adharma, grown large through your negligence, swallows us like a serpent; and it enlarges the side of the suras, nurtured by the divine order."

sanskrit: viṣayeṣu prasaktena yatkiṃcitkāriṇā tvayā ṛṣīṇām agnikalpānām udvego janito mahān teṣāṃ prabhāvo durdharṣaḥ pradīpta iva pāvakaḥ
english: "By you, who are given over to sense-pleasures and who acts impulsively, great distress has been caused to the sages who are like fire; their blazing power is irresistible, like a kindled conflagration."

sanskrit: tapasā bhāvitātmāno dharmasyānugrahe ratāḥ mukhyair yajñair yajanty ete nityaṃ tais tair dvijātayaḥ
english: "These twice-born ones, whose souls are refined by austerity and who delight in sustaining Dharma, worship perpetually with foremost sacrifices of every kind."

sanskrit: juhvaty agnīṃś ca vidhivad vedāṃś coccair adhīyate abhibhūya ca rakṣāṃsi brahmaghoṣān udairayan diśo vipradrutāḥ sarve stanayitnur ivoṣṇage
english: "They pour oblations into the sacred fires according to rule and chant the Vedas aloud; overpowering the rākṣasas, they raise the thunder of the brahman-sound, scattering in all directions like thunderclouds in the hot season."

sanskrit: ṛṣīṇām agnikalpānām agnihotrasamutthitaḥ ādatte rakṣasāṃ tejo dhūmo vyāpya diśo daśa
english: "The smoke that rises from the Agnihotra of those sages who are like fire, pervading all ten directions, draws away the vitality of the rākṣasas."

sanskrit: teṣu teṣu ca deśeṣu puṇyeṣu ca dṛḍhavrataiḥ caryamāṇaṃ tapas tīvraṃ saṃtāpayati rākṣasān
english: "And in those various sacred regions, the fierce austerity practised by those firm in their vows torments the rākṣasas."

sanskrit: utpātān vividhān dṛṣṭvā ghorān bahuvidhāṃs tathā vināśam anupaśyāmi sarveṣāṃ rakṣasām aham
english: "Having seen the many and various dreadful portents of every kind, I foresee the destruction of all the rākṣasas."

sanskrit: kharābhis tanitā ghorā meghāḥ pratibhayaṃkaraḥ śoṇitenābhivarṣanti laṅkām uṣṇena sarvataḥ
english: "Dreadful and terrifying clouds thunder harshly, and they rain warm blood upon Laṅkā from every direction."

sanskrit: rudatāṃ vāhanānāṃ ca prapatanty asrabindavaḥ dhvajā dhvastā vivarṇāś ca na prabhānti yathāpuram
english: "Tears fall from the weeping draught-animals; the banners have fallen and are discoloured and do not gleam as before."

sanskrit: vyālā gomāyavo gṛdhrā vāśanti ca subhairavam śreyo na paśyanti nṛpasya doṣaiḥ praviśya laṅkām aniśaṃ samavāyāṃś ca kurvate
english: "Wolves, jackals, and vultures cry out most dreadfully; they enter Laṅkā incessantly and gather in assemblies."

sanskrit: kālikāḥ pāṇḍurair dantaiḥ prahasanty agrataḥ sthitāḥ striyaḥ svapneṣu muṣṇantyo gṛhāṇi pratibhāṣya ca
english: "Dark-complexioned women with white teeth stand in front and laugh; and in dreams women despoil houses and jeer at them."

sanskrit: gṛhāṇāṃ balikarmāṇi śvānaḥ paryupabhuñjate kharā goṣu prajāyante mūṣikā nakulaiḥ saha
english: "Dogs devour the offering-oblations of households; donkeys are born of cows; rats consort with mongooses."

sanskrit: mārjārā dvīpibhiḥ sārdhaṃ sūkarāḥ śunakaiḥ saha kiṃnarā rākṣasaiś cāpi sameyur mānuṣaiḥ saha
english: "Cats couple with leopards; pigs with dogs; kiṃnaras meet with rākṣasas, and rākṣasas with humans."

sanskrit: pāṇḍurā raktapādāś ca vihagāḥ kālacoditāḥ rākṣasānāṃ vināśāya kapotā vicaranti ca
english: "Pale birds with red feet, impelled by fate, and doves, wander about for the destruction of the rākṣasas."

sanskrit: cīkī kūcīti vāśantyaḥ śārikā veśmasu sthitāḥ patanti grathitāś cāpi nirjitāḥ kalahaiṣiṇaḥ
english: "Mynas perched in the houses cry 'cīkī kūcī'; and the quarrelsome ones, vanquished, fall down entangled together."

sanskrit: karālo vikaṭo muṇḍaḥ puruṣaḥ kṛṣṇapiṅgalaḥ kālo gṛhāṇi sarveṣāṃ kāle kāle 'nvavekṣate etāny anyāni duṣṭāni nimittāny utpatanti ca
english: "A dreadful, misshapen, bald man, dark-tawny in colour — Time itself — surveys everyone's houses again and again at the appointed hour; and these and other evil omens keep arising."

sanskrit: viṣṇuṃ manyāmahe rāmaṃ mānuṣaṃ deham āsthitam na hi mānuṣamātro 'sau rāghavo dṛḍhavikramaḥ
english: "We believe Rāma to be Viṣṇu himself, who has assumed a human body; for that Rāghava of firm prowess is not a mere human being."

sanskrit: yena baddhaḥ samudrasya sa setuḥ paramādbhutaḥ kuruṣva nararājena saṃdhiṃ rāmeṇa rāvaṇa
english: "By whom that most wondrous bridge across the ocean has been built — make peace with that king of men, Rāma, O Rāvaṇa."

sanskrit: idaṃ vacas tatra nigadya mālyavan parīkṣya rakṣo'dhipater manaḥ punaḥ anuttameṣūttamapauruṣo balī babhūva tūṣṇīṃ samavekṣya rāvaṇam
english: Having spoken these words there and gauging the mind of the lord of rākṣasas, Mālyavān — that powerful one of supreme manly prowess among the greatest — fell silent and waited, watching Rāvaṇa.

sanskrit: tat tu mālyavato vākyaṃ hitam uktaṃ daśānanaḥ na marṣayati duṣṭātmā kālasya vaśam āgataḥ
english: But that beneficial speech spoken by Mālyavān, the ten-faced one, evil-souled and fallen under the sway of Time, did not receive with patience.

sanskrit: sa baddhvā bhrukuṭiṃ vaktre krodhasya vaśam āgataḥ amarṣāt parivṛttākṣo mālyavantam athābravīt
english: He, having knitted his brows on his face, having come under the sway of anger, his eyes rolling with indignation, then spoke to Mālyavān.

sanskrit: hitabuddhyā yad ahitaṃ vacaḥ paruṣam ucyate parapakṣaṃ praviśyaiva naitac chrotragataṃ mama
english: "That harsh speech which is spoken with an ostensibly beneficial intention but is actually harmful, spoken by one who has gone over to the enemy's side — this does not enter my ears."

sanskrit: mānuṣaṃ kṛpaṇaṃ rāmam ekaṃ śākhāmṛgāśrayam samarthaṃ manyase kena tyaktaṃ pitrā vanālayam
english: "By what reasoning do you consider that wretched Rāma, a mere human, alone and dependent on tree-dwelling monkeys, abandoned by his father to a forest dwelling, to be capable?"

sanskrit: rakṣasām īśvaraṃ māṃ ca devatānāṃ bhayaṃkaram hīnaṃ māṃ manyase kena ahīnaṃ sarvavikramaiḥ
english: "By what reasoning do you consider me, lord of the rākṣasas and cause of terror to the gods, to be inferior — me who is not inferior in any of the heroic arts?"

sanskrit: vīradveṣeṇa vā śaṅke pakṣapātena vā ripoḥ tvayāhaṃ paruṣāṇy uktaḥ paraprotsāhanena vā
english: "I suspect you have spoken these harsh words to me out of hatred for heroes, out of partiality toward the enemy, or out of encouragement by the other side."

sanskrit: prabhavantaṃ padasthaṃ hi paruṣaṃ ko 'bhidhāsyati paṇḍitaḥ śāstratattvajño vinā protsāhanād ripoḥ
english: "For who among the learned, who know the essence of the scriptures, would speak harshly to one who is powerful and established in his position, without being instigated by the enemy?"

sanskrit: ānīya ca vanāt sītāṃ padmahīnām iva śriyam kimarthaṃ pratidāsyāmi rāghavasya bhayād aham
english: "Having brought Sītā from the forest — like Śrī deprived of her lotus — why should I return her out of fear of Rāghava?"

sanskrit: vṛtaṃ vānarakoṭībhiḥ sasugrīvaṃ salakṣmaṇam paśya kaiś cid ahobhis tvaṃ rāghavaṃ nihataṃ mayā
english: "Within a few days you shall see Rāghava together with Sugrīva and Lakṣmaṇa, surrounded by tens of millions of vānaras, slain by me."

sanskrit: dvandve yasya na tiṣṭhanti daivatāny api saṃyuge sa kasmād rāvaṇo yuddhe bhayam āhārayiṣyati
english: "Rāvaṇa, before whom even the gods do not stand firm in single combat and in battle — why should he harbour fear in war?"

sanskrit: dvidhā bhajyeyam apy evaṃ na nameyaṃ tu kasya cit eṣa me sahajo doṣaḥ svabhāvo duratikramaḥ
english: "I would sooner be split in two than bow to anyone; this is an innate fault in me, a nature difficult to overcome."

sanskrit: yadi tāvat samudre tu setur baddho yadṛcchayā rāmeṇa vismayaḥ ko 'tra yena te bhayam āgatam
english: "And if a bridge was built across the ocean by Rāma merely by chance, what wonder is there in that, that fear has come upon you because of it?"

sanskrit: sa tu tīrtvārṇavaṃ rāmaḥ saha vānarasenayā pratijānāmi te satyaṃ na jīvan pratiyāsyati
english: "But that Rāma, having crossed the ocean with his vānara army — I promise you truly he shall not return alive."

sanskrit: evaṃ bruvāṇaṃ saṃrabdhaṃ ruṣṭaṃ vijñāya rāvaṇam vrīḍito mālyavān vākyaṃ nottaraṃ pratyapadyata
english: Recognizing Rāvaṇa as he spoke thus, inflamed and enraged, Mālyavān, abashed, did not offer any reply.

sanskrit: jayāśiṣā ca rājānaṃ vardhayitvā yathocitam mālyavān abhyanujñāto jagāma svaṃ niveśanam
english: Having duly pronounced the benediction of victory upon the king in the fitting manner, Mālyavān, having received leave to depart, went to his own dwelling.

sanskrit: rāvaṇas tu sahāmātyo mantrayitvā vimṛśya ca laṅkāyām atulāṃ guptiṃ kārayām āsa rākṣasaḥ
english: But Rāvaṇa the rākṣasa, having deliberated and reflected together with his ministers, caused the incomparable fortification of Laṅkā to be arranged.

sanskrit: vyādideśa ca pūrvasyāṃ prahastaṃ dvāri rākṣasaṃ dakṣiṇasyāṃ mahāvīryau mahāpārśva mahodarau
english: He assigned the rākṣasa Prahasta to the eastern gate, and the two great-valiant ones, Mahāpārśva and Mahōdara, to the southern gate.

sanskrit: paścimāyām atho dvāri putram indrajitaṃ tathā vyādideśa mahāmāyaṃ rākṣasair bahubhir vṛtam
english: And to the western gate he likewise assigned his son Indrajit, the master of great illusion, surrounded by many rākṣasas.

sanskrit: uttarasyāṃ puradvāri vyādiśya śukasāraṇau svayaṃ cātra bhaviṣyāmi mantriṇas tān uvāca ha
english: Having assigned Śuka and Sāraṇa to the northern city gate, he said to those ministers: "I myself shall be here."

sanskrit: rākṣasaṃ tu virūpākṣaṃ mahāvīryaparākramam madhyame 'sthāpayad gulme bahubhiḥ saha rākṣasaiḥ
english: And the rākṣasa Virūpākṣa, of great might and valour, he stationed in the central reserve force together with many rākṣasas.

sanskrit: evaṃvidhānaṃ laṅkāyāṃ kṛtvā rākṣasapuṃgavaḥ mene kṛtārtham ātmānaṃ kṛtāntavaśam āgataḥ
english: Having made these arrangements for Laṅkā, that bull among rākṣasas considered his purpose accomplished — though he had come under the sway of Fate.

sanskrit: visarjayām āsa tataḥ sa mantriṇo vidhānam ājñāpya purasya puṣkalam jayāśiṣā mantragaṇena pūjito viveśa so 'ntaḥpuram ṛddhiman mahat
english: He then dismissed the ministers having commanded the complete arrangement of the city's defence; honoured with benedictions of victory and hymns by the assembly of counsellors, he entered his great and opulent inner palace.
